paragraphs.text: POEMS ATTRIBUTED TO ORIENTIUS
I. ON THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD
A light more splendid than light shines out, and, greater than other days,
a bright day gleams, more festive than all the rest of the year,
the birthday chosen by God, on which he is born
who reigns forever with the Father in the fellowship of heaven,
the Father's great power, taking the first beginnings of our flesh,
and soon, his death accomplished, carrying man back into heaven,
he who willed to take on flesh, and yet does not grow old in the flesh.
II. ON THE TITLES OF OUR SAVIOUR
Door, Virgin, Lion, Power, Wisdom, Word,
King, Staff, Prince, Leader, Rock, Shepherd, Man,
Nets, Sun, Bridegroom, Seed, Mountain, Star, Teacher,
Pearl, Day, Lamb, Sheep, Calf,
Treasure, Fountain, Life, Hand, Head, Fire, Plough,
Flower, Cornerstone, Right Hand, Column [?], Child,
Gentle One, Adam, Finger, Mirror, Way, Grape-cluster, Bread,
Victim, Law, Reason, Rod, Fish, Eagle,
the Just One, the Offspring of the King and the King's Priest:
great names for God, but God himself is greater.
III. ALSO BY THE SAME AUTHOR: ON THE TRINITY
That which was from the ages, and which is to the ages of ages,
will always be, because it always was; it is, and abides without end.
Above all that exists, without which nothing is, to which all things belong,
the all-begetting Word, the Word, almighty God [?],
who alone with the Father, with whom the Father and God [?] alone:
this was, when nature had not yet received its origin.
For Christ is the seed, Christ the first beginning of things,
Christ the honour of the earth, the dread of the world, the glory of heaven,
from God the Ruler, King and Ruler [?] on high,
the only one begotten before all, but begotten of that Father
whom no one begot, through whom all things that beget exist:
[?] we beseech him, long for him, tremble before him, revere him, love him.
Whole and from the whole, spread through the whole world;
not the same, and yet wholly the same, both alike and together,
equal in measure and equal in rank: so Son and Father are one;
the name is divided by name, the substance is united,
completing the holy mysteries of the sacred deep.
A mighty fullness, given over to itself, bound each to each in turn,
the threefold union of powers is made equal,
and the Spirit, hovering, is the whole perfection on high.
So the honour in Christ is the Father's praise; in the Father it is Christ's.
He is the Father's mind and word and witness and heir;
he knows how much the Father ventures in him;
he is our head, our wisdom, grace and life;
he is the guardian of mankind, its watchman, and he its judge;
he is the road of salvation, and he the unchanging light,
true splendour from the true, light from light,
good from goodness, full from the full and rich,
provident, forgiving, merciful, compassionate, bountiful,
perfect, patient, just, loving, spotless,
the eternal gift of the Eternal, the protection of those of old,
the soul's firm support, the demon's rout, the weapons of faith,
reigning forever, assessor and judge of what is to come,
not shut in by time, who will shut up the times at his command,
beginning and end, the quickener within and without,
holding the will and mighty in power, stern in his gentleness,
the peace and joy of the world, who parts the wicked from the good.
A man who bears two natures, and the mediator,
while as God he proved immortal what is mortal.
O blessed lordship of the Lord, O noble death!
O hard heart and faithless error of a wretched nation!
Impious condemner, your death hangs on this stake;
believing confessor, your life will live by this blood.
You are swayed [?] as God [?] judges, who, though he seemed to punish,
saved the peoples, he whom the unjust people [?] hated.
This is he who was first rejected by his own, and accursed,
spat upon by men, the reproach of a mob doomed to perish.
This is he for whom a cruel hand poured out gall mixed with vinegar,
whom blows of the palm outraged with blind beating.
Look, mad assailant, at the venerable wood;
see the victorious tokens of the blood you profaned.
Is he not the living God, God unconquerable by the foe,
vengeance, refuge, rest, light, life, faith, hope?
From the Father he is to be known as sower and giver of life;
from the cross, as avenger and the one who drives back hell,
who washes away errors, our sure peace, our generous pardon.
Born out of love for man, he suffered for the sake of salvation,
fulfilled the law of death, and rose alive again into the lofty heavens,
seated on his Father's throne, the bringer of salvation above every age,
from where he deigned to visit the lowly earth, able to return there again.
The price of sin, himself knowing nothing of sin,
sharing in his servants, conforming them to himself when glorified.
See how beautiful a trophy shines for you across our thresholds,
O Christ; how bright the banners you carry back to the Father,
still stained with blood, and yet, as before, ever
mighty in power, everlasting in majesty.
Yet why the form set before us should bear this shape of the cross
the figure, to be adored in every respect, makes plain.
Since the sign stands out divided into four parts,
it lets us know the Lord of the world [?] and all the archangels.
He rules as many regions as the borders of heaven the cross looks upon.
The cross imitates the devout palms of one at prayer;
the cross, bearing witness to God, depicts [?] peace, and is peace,
the peace given through the wood: peace is held written on the wood.
Would you, admirer, also look at the Greek figures?
See the perfect riddle of this rich sign.
You may see a Greek P: that is the head, or the arms of the one nailed there.
The Iota, standing upright, is here the hanging of the body.
The letter proclaims punishment; the punishment brings salvation.
Next to it, then, is Alpha, and close by stands the other, Omega:
the first because he is the first, the last because he is the last.
These are the elements of the letters; God here is above every element:
all the emblems agree with the heavenly sign.
When he mounts the wood, God shows that the wood is
the stuff of fruit; when he stretches out its branch on high,
the Lord, higher than the heights, towers over all.
He is the middle of those nailed up: the number three gives him honour.
He is pierced, and gore flows out; water [?] from the wound that was made
comes out, and soon from that same wound blood. Surely
the blood is martyrdom, and the water claims for itself the washing of baptism.
So by divine power death came by a tree, and life came too.
By the fruit, first-made man, you fall; by the cross, O Christ, you heal:
there the pestilent serpent [?] offered the deadly food.
No wonder, then, if manifold praise draws out a thousand names,
scarcely worthy of God, a praise unequal to such great powers,
as many titles as the miracles of the holy Christ have brought forth.
EXPLANATION OF THE NAMES OF THE LORD
Door, because he dwells in heaven and opens its secrets.
Virgin, for his birth has its origin in an undefiled mother.
And Lion: he is King of kings; the lion is called
king of beasts. And Power: nothing is stronger than he alone.
But why is he called Wisdom? He is the rule of life.
How is he the Word? Because he flowed from the Father's mouth.
Why is he now King and now the King's Son?
Because with the Father he holds the throne of heaven in common.
Why Staff? Because he lifts up the fallen and raises the sick.
Why Prince? Because he governs all things subject to his throne.
Why Leader of the heavenly army? From the holy host.
Why Rock? Because he sets things firm on a strong foundation.
Why the Good Shepherd? Because he wards [?] off blemish from the sheepfolds.
Now Man: for he was born and took flesh from a virgin.
Why Nets? Because he gathers the scattered nations from everywhere.
Why Sun of Righteousness? Because he enlightens every righteous person.
Why Bridegroom? Because the virgin Church is betrothed to God.
Why Holy [?]? Because he sows blessed kingdoms with his word.
Mountain: because its heights do not yield to everyone who climbs.
Star: because with his guiding light he directs uncertain journeys [?].
Why Teacher? He loves to teach hearts that serve him.
Pearl: what could be found more precious than this?
Why Day? Because he shines more [?] than light.
Then, because he is holy [?], he is held to be the innocent Lamb,
who alone could take away the sin of the world.
And now he is called Sheep, because he yields himself to those who slaughter him;
and he is called Calf: the passion he endured shows this.
Fountain, because he cleanses vice with abundant baptism.
Life, because he gives those he quickens eternal life.
He is Hand: the rich working of his mighty deeds meets us.
He is Head: it is plain, for by him as author we are created.
Fire: in this, that our testing still remains.
Why Plough [?]? Because he breaks up hearts and makes them fruitful.
Flower, because he himself crowns confessors and martyrs.
Why Cornerstone? Because he binds both peoples together.
Right Hand, because he sits at the Father's side, adorning and honouring it.
Often Dove: because he knows no guile and is without gall.
Why Child? Because he goes pure to his Father's citadel.
Vine: because he propagates himself through an adopted heir.
Why second Adam? Because he himself is the head of the reborn.
He is Finger, that pen: God's law is written through him.
Now Mirror: because the image of the Father shines through in him.
Now Way: because he goes before the saints into paradise.
Grape-cluster: because he waters the world with heavenly juices.
Bread: in this, that he is the nourishment of our faith.
Why is he a living Victim to God, and himself the High Priest?
Because, sanctifying himself, he offers himself on his Father's altars.
Now Reason: this is the reason by which the fabric of the world stands.
Rod: because, as with a lash, he corrects the doings of those who stray.
Fish, born of the waters: he himself is the author of baptism.
Often Eagle: since like a bird he flew back up from the earth.
PRAISE
Finally, so as not to linger over so many great things with many words:
he is Eye: I know God, and God sees every heart.
Why Prophet? Because he reveals in brief [?] what is to come.
Why Angel? Because he himself was his own messenger.
He is called Arm, from the embrace with which he holds all things.
Whatever it is by which you are called, Holy One, I acknowledge that it is yours.
The greatness of his works hides the names of so many things,
but such great honours are reckoned by their own merits.
The reason makes the titles; power lets the names be known.
You, seated on high, are Hagios, our blessing.
You are God Emmanuel: the Godhead dwelling with us.
You, Lord Sabaoth, shield with your fist all that exists anywhere.
You the house of Israel and the blessed confessors,
you all the patriarchs, and you every angel adore.
You flash above the [?] cherubim, above the stars;
you who were promised to Abraham, of the seed of David,
worthy of praise, you hear the glorious Hosanna in heaven [?].
Only look upon us, crucified one, Paraclete, Christ,
Nazarene; God in whom we believe, and Galilean,
and God of Abraham our holy father, and God of Isaac,
and gracious God of Jacob, from whom come our hope and our faith.
Look upon your own, O Christ, and long protect the redeemed.
I, unworthy, make my plea; but deign to hear me as I ask,
Almighty, have mercy on me, have mercy on those dear to me; grant
that grief may depart, that care and fear may take their leave,
that your servant may be joined with the saints, and that I may fear you
and please you while I live, and not be found guilty at that
time when I shall stand, mindful of my deserts, before your judgment seat,
O Christ; and may I truly worship the Godhead that I proclaim.
Your cross on my brow, my hand, my lips; may the cross settle deep within me.
May the cross be the shield of my house, the cross the breastplate of salvation.
With this sign the shining tower will gleam more brightly
than when, defiled, it was drenched with sacrilegious blood.
